article_text:
The cult magazine by artist Maurizio Cattelan and photographer Pierpaolo Ferrari makes its return this autumn with Damiani Books, bringing a new issue of images as inventive as they are sharp, and an exhibition in Shenzhen, China.

By Guénola Pellen. Photos by Toiletpaper.

The 21st edition of Toiletpaper opens with a cover that conjures Martin Parr’s grotesque vision of summer leisure and the streak of bad taste that is the magazine’s hallmark. An elderly woman photographed from behind, blue swimsuit, pink plastic bag on her arm: her scarlet back reveals, in negative, a smiley face of unburned skin. Maurizio Cattelan, iconoclastic provocateur of the contemporary art world, and Pierpaolo Ferrari, art director whose practice blends fashion, advertising and surrealism, staged every inch of it.

The editorial venture was born of their first collaboration for W Magazine in 2009. “We had so much fun, we said, why don’t we do more of this?” Maurizio Cattelan told The New Yorker in 2011. Toiletpaper launched the following year: not a word, not an advertisement. Every image is built entirely in camera, meticulously staged tableaux vivants with saturated chromatism that subvert the codes of advertising, fashion and cinema.

“We keep homing in on what a Toiletpaper image is. Like distilling a perfume. It’s not about one particular style or time frame; what makes them Toiletpaper is a special twist. An uncanny ambiguity,” Maurizio Cattelan told The New Yorker in the same interview. In this edition, a monkey wrench locks itself around an ear, a fuchsia stiletto brims with a banana split in an equivocal nod to food porn, and a chef’s knife is held upside down, its bare blade turned toward the very hand that brandishes it: chic, precise and sovereignly unsettling.

Published three years after its predecessor, the issue is accompanied by an exhibition at the Fotografiska museum in Shenzhen, China, and a limited-edition 2027 calendar created with German photographer Ellen von Unwerth, high priestess of fashion and glamour photography.

Toiletpaper Magazine 21 , by Maurizio Cattelan and Pierpaolo Ferrari, is published by Damiani Books , 40 pages, softcover, $20. “ToiletFotoPaperGrafiska” , Toiletpaper’s first exhibition in China, runs from October 1st, 2026 to March 14, 2027 at Fotografiska Shenzhen .

title_original: BAFTA Launches Review Over Concerns About Trustees Accepting Free Awards Guest Tickets
editorial_title_zh: BAFTA启动审查，因受托人接受免费颁奖典礼嘉宾门票引发担忧

article_text:
BAFTA has launched a review after its trustees were accused of potentially breaching UK charity law by accepting free guest tickets to awards ceremonies.

During BAFTA’s annual general meeting this week, Michael Pritchett, an independent film producer who serves as the elected chair of BAFTA’s membership council, raised concerns about whether trustees broke rules that prevent them from receiving remuneration or benefits.

Pritchett alleged that trustees had received complimentary tickets for themselves and a guest at BAFTA’s film, television, and games awards, according to a transcription of his remarks seen by Deadline. He claimed that the custom had been ongoing for up to 20 years, with guests receiving top-table tickets potentially worth up to £2,000 ($2,665) for the film awards.

Related Stories

BAFTA Names New Chair

BAFTA Makes Plans For 'I Swear's John Davidson To Attend Scotland Awards After N-Word Scandal

Pritchett — who said he had been privately raising concerns with BAFTA officials for months — added that trustees approved accounts, which state that no trustees received any remuneration during the year for their services.

Watch on Deadline

Speaking at the AGM, Pritchett said he had paid for legal advice at his own expense, which concluded that “offenses under the Charities Act and the Companies Act are likely to have been committed by the trustees who approved those accounts.”

Pritchett also raised questions over whether BAFTA had properly paid tax on the tickets. “Since 2016, a benefit like this is likely to have been taxable, with National Insurance payable by BAFTA. BAFTA has not told me that anything has ever been reported. So I can’t assure you whether it has or hasn’t,” he said.

BAFTA stopped offering plus-one tickets to trustees last year following a recommendation from its governance committee. It has now launched a review of ticketing arrangements, which is being led by a group of three unnamed industry executives.

A BAFTA spokesperson said: “Trustees of BAFTA are invited to attend events in a working capacity, representing the Academy in an ambassadorial role, and prior to 2025 they could also bring a ‘plus one’ guest to accompany them.

“In 2025 BAFTA decided to review its guest tickets arrangements and discontinued the long-standing custom and practice of trustees inviting a plus one. The board has since established an independent review group to consider the historic guest ticket arrangement – the review is underway.”

BAFTA stands by the practice of offering trustees themselves free tickets, believing it is part of their duties to attend events and act as ambassadors for the charity. BAFTA’s trustees, who provide their services voluntarily, include new chair, Hilary Rosen.

Pritchett was also critical of BAFTA’s refusal to hand over records of who had received free awards tickets. He said his request was refused by a senior BAFTA executive, with “no policy cited.”

During the annual general meeting, Sara Putt, BAFTA’s former chair, revealed that the Academy had obtained its own legal advice based on a fuller picture of the ticketing issue. This has not been shared with Pritchett or other members.

Pritchett told members: “Last year, you paid £4.7 million in membership fees. The records belong to the charity that you subscribe to. And if the person you elected can be refused those records, citing no rule, then the right to see anything is gone forever. Not just for me, but for anyone who holds this office after me.”

He concluded: “I would simply now say to any trustee in the future, as I’d say to any trustee of any charity: Will you obey the law, pay any taxes due, and pay back anything that is due? Correct the accounts, open the records to the committee as the rules require.”

The Guardian first reported on the events at BAFTA’s annual general meeting.

article_text:
奈良の秋の風物詩「正倉院展」では、グッズショップ巡りも定番コースになりつつあります。今年も館内のショップと、会場を出てすぐのところにある屋外の特設ショップ「天平」の2か所で、それぞれ異なる商品が販売されています。お土産にぴったりのお菓子から普段使いできそうなアイテムまで、多彩なラインナップがそろっていました。

奈良国立博物館内ミュージアムショップ 毎年、勅封が解かれるのに合わせて開催される正倉院展では、その年の出陳宝物をモチーフにしたグッズを楽しみにされているファンも多いのではないでしょうか。

「第78回」の思い出に Wクリアファイル 660円など

第78回の今回は、ポスターでも取り上げられている「 漆胡瓶 」や、「 紅牙撥鏤碁子 」「 紺牙撥鏤碁子 」などのグッズが目立ちました。

山中塗りステンレスボトル 3850円

「漆胡瓶」に描かれた文様を切り出してデザインされたステンレスボトルです。140ミリ・リットルと持ち運びに便利なミニサイズで、これからの季節、温かいものをちょっと飲みたいときに重宝しそう。写真の黒色と白色の2色展開です。

トートバッグ 1650円

こちらも漆胡瓶を描いたトートバッグです。肩ひもが長めのデザイン。

特設ショップ「天平」 奈良国立博物館から出て、すぐ目の前にある特設ショップ「天平」へ。こちらもお見逃しなく。

“天平のモノグラム” ロングストール 7920円

ミュージアムが大好きなメンバーが集まる通信販売「フェリシモ」の「ミュージアム部」から、おしゃれなアイテムが登場しました。「 紫檀木画槽琵琶 ロングストール」は、花菱の文様が交互に配され、どこか高級メゾンのアイテムを思わせます。紫地と淡い水色を基調にした薄手の綿が重ねられており、どちらの面も装いのアクセントになりそうです。

チョコレート缶 1296円など

天平もお菓子が充実しています。缶の蓋をスライドさせると、中のチョコレートは「紅牙撥鏤碁子」「紺牙撥鏤碁子」そのもの！ 碁子に描かれた「 花喰鳥 」を表した飴はいちごミルク味で10粒入り864円、漆胡瓶の巾着の中身はクランチチョコレート（1080円）です。

清浄歓喜団 1620円

奈良時代に唐から伝わった「唐菓子」は、和菓子の源流とも言われます。そのひとつ、京都の老舗・亀屋清永が手がける「清浄歓喜団」の正倉院展バージョンが登場しました。白檀などのお香を練り込んだこしあんを包み、ごま油で揚げてあるそうです。巾着のような形の底に親指をあて、押し上げて割っていただきます。聖武天皇も宮中の儀礼などで口にしたことがあるでしょうか。そんな思いを巡らせながら、ぜひお試しください。

カラフルプリントタオルハンカチ 1540円

店内でひときわ目をひくカラフルさ！ 「ときめきあふれるステーショナリー」を届けるGreenFlashとのコラボで、正倉院正倉を中心に、さまざまな宝物やその文様がデザインされています。A4クリアファイル（825円）は中で3層に仕切られていて便利です。

ピンバッジ 990円

最後にショップ担当イチオシをご紹介。「細かい文様の再現にこだわりました」というピンバッジです。

※商品は完売や入荷待ちの場合もありますので、あらかじめご了承ください。

（読売新聞美術展ナビ編集班）

正倉院展のチケットは美術展ナビチケットアプリ（スマホ）で好評発売中

第78回 正倉院展

会場：奈良国立博物館 東西新館（奈良市登大路町50 奈良公園内）

会期：2026年10月24日（土）～11月9日（月）

休館日：会期中は無休

開館時間：8:00～18:00 ※金土日祝は20時まで （入場は閉館の60分前まで）

観覧料（日時指定券）：一般2,000円（1,500円）、高大生1,500円（1,000円）、小中生500円（無料）、キャンパスメンバーズ学生400円 ※カッコ内はレイト割料金（月～木は16時以降、金～日と祝日は17時以降） 日時指定枠に空きがある場合には、博物館敷地内の特設窓口にて当日の「日時指定券」を販売するが、1枚ごとに200円の発券料がかかる。

詳しくは正倉院展公式サイト（ https://shosoin-ten.jp/ ）、 博物館公式ホームページ へ。

◇「第78回 正倉院展」（奈良国立博物館）徹底ガイド 10月24日から11月9日まで 見どころからグッズまで

以下は開幕記事です。

古都奈良の秋の風物詩「第78回 正倉院展」が奈良国立博物館(奈良公園内)で10月24日（土）から11月9日（月）まで開催されます。開幕前日の報道内覧会を取材しました。今年はシルクロードを感じさせる宝物が特に充実していました。

正倉院の神秘性を示す異色の宝物「龍（ニホンテン）のミイラ」

週末の正倉院展、雨予報で「残念…」と思っている方も多いと思います。ただ、今回は足利義満が宝庫を拝見した時、義教が蘭奢待を切り取った時など、開検のたびに雨が降る”原因”とされた「 虹龍 」（ニホンテンのミイラ）が出陳されています。雨もまた正倉院の神秘に触れる一つの演出かもしれません。

◇虹龍の調査については下の記事の中ほどで詳しく↓

館内、館外（天平）の２つの特設ショップもパワーアップ！

article_text:
The surly miser Ebenezer Scrooge is no longer just a fictional character haunting the holidays — he’s on Venmo .

To promote Ti West’s upcoming adaptation of the notorious character in the film “Ebenezer,” starring Johnny Depp in the titular role, the Paramount promotional team created a Venmo account for Ebenezer Scrooge. The official account for the film announced the news on X , writing, “Ebenezer Scrooge is now on @venmo. Think he’s feeling generous? 💰 Send a request: https://venmo.com/u/EBENEZERmovie ” accompanied by a video of people making requests for various amounts of money and Scrooge’s stingy payouts. Despite the request, Ebenezer’s response is always the same, giving just a penny in return.

Related Stories

Crime Thriller ‘Side Effects’ Debuts First-Look Photos and Warns About the ‘Real Killer on the Loose’: Deadly Opioids (EXCLUSIVE)

Fremantle Appoints Sharon Levy as Head of Americas and Australia

An error message reading, “We’re sorry the transaction could not be completed. Please contact the person you’re trying to pay” appeared when two Variety staffers tried to request some money. A source close to promotion confirmed that the Venmo has been working — it just grew so popular with requests that it temporarily caused a jam in the system and is being fixed.

Popular on Variety

Although Scrooge’s Venmo is dishing out money, he also appears to be accepting it. The public feed of his account is filled with payments made out to him. “For cheers and joy! (And maybe a little luck please)” one benefactor wrote. Another wrote, “$ Retainer Fee — for the Ghost of Christmas Past to haunt my exes with a little bah humbug spirit.” Several others paid Scrooge to boost his Christmas spirit.

It is unclear where this sent money will actually end up.

Paramount Pictures’ “Ebenezer” will hit theaters on Nov. 13. The official logline reads: “The name you know, the story you don’t.” Judging from the trailer, West — known for directing the horror trilogy “X” — is zooming in on the darker aspects of Charles Dickens’ beloved story, showing Depp’s character being haunted by some seriously scary ghosts and getting buried alive.

Depp stars alongside Rupert Grint, Andrea Riseborough, Sam Claflin, Daisy Ridley, Arthur Conti, Ellie Bamber, Henry Lloyd-Hughes, Charlie Murphy, Tramell Tillman and Ian McKellen. Based on “A Christmas Carol” by Charles Dickens, Nathaniel Halpern adapted the screenplay.

“Ebenezer” marks Depp’s return home to Hollywood for the holidays as his first major movie since his highly publicized 2022 trial against ex-wife Amber Heard. Both Depp and Heard accused the other of domestic abuse and defamation during their relationship, with Depp ultimately awarded $10 million in compensatory damages and $5 million in punitive damages from Heard, while Heard was awarded $2 million in compensatory damages. His last major Hollywood studio film was “Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald” in 2018.

editorial_excerpt_zh: 这位低调的行业老兵最初以流行二人组彼得与戈登（Peter and Gordon）成员身份出道，后转为制作詹姆斯·泰勒（James Taylor）和琳达·罗德斯坦（Linda Ronstadt）等音乐人的金牌制作人，其幕后故事揭晓。摇滚乐向来以恶劣行为的故事而臭名昭著：把电视机扔出窗外、成山的古柯碱……

Asher），看起来可以说是60年代/70年代音乐行业老兵中最书呆子气、生活最检点的一位了。尽管这或许正是他想让我们这么认为的；阿什在镜头之外会不会是个彻底的浪荡子，而只是极其擅长掩饰呢？那副眼镜与荷叶边衬衫的搭配，确实让人想起某个略显油滑的人，甚至在阿什本人在片尾字幕中提及这一点之前就有这种感觉。", "links": [{"text": "James Taylor", "url": "无论真相如何，阿什以任何标准来看都开辟了一条令人惊叹的道路，将身处正确时间和正确地点的优势发挥到了极致。影片围绕阿什的“轶事与音乐”现场演出巧妙结构，将剪辑片段、音频和音乐表演交织在一起，快速闪过他的个人背景故事。他最幸运的突破，当然是早期与校友戈登·瓦勒（Gordon Waller）的组合（事实证明，该组合是以埃弗利兄弟为蓝本）受益于他姐姐的男友、保罗·麦卡特尼（Paul McCartney）赠予的被弃用歌曲；其中有一个有趣的时刻，我们听到约翰·列侬（John Lennon）对后来成为彼得与戈登第一首也是最大热门歌曲《A World Without Love》歌词的嘲弄：“请把我锁起来……”“是的”。虽然影片明确承认了对麦卡特尼歌曲创作的债务（列侬大概曾为披头士否决了这首歌），但它或许还没准备好承认，如果没有这种联系，之后发生的一切将根本不会存在。", "阿什曾在某个时刻表示自己算不上什么流行歌星，随后的事件表明他大概是对的。他似乎在聚光灯之外感到更自在，这让他得以成为摇摆的60年代伦敦披头士圈子里无处不在的人物，正如片名所暗示的那样。他是超酷艺术画廊Indica的联合所有者（列侬正是在那里第一次遇到了小野洋子），不过考虑到它只维持了两年，或许他在那方面也不是那么出色。然而，正是在披头士的关系中，当他被任命为新成立的苹果唱片（Apple Records）艺人与 repertoire (A&R) 主管、并在萨维尔罗（Savile Row）大楼拥有自己的顶层办公室时，他才真正迎来了属于自己的高光时刻。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿什的发掘对象是泰勒，后者在美国老家毫无进展后迁居伦敦；在制作了泰勒的首张专辑（他以特有的谦逊称自己把这张专辑用披头士风格的管弦乐给搞砸了）之后，阿什跟随泰勒前往洛杉矶，并作为一名制作人和经纪人，悄然开启了令人印象深刻的第二人生涯。在制作了泰勒的突破性第二张专辑《Sweet Baby James》之后，阿什成为了20世纪70年代加州轻摇滚的关键人物，监管了包括安德鲁·戈尔德（Andrew Gold）、凯特·泰勒（Kate Taylor）、JD·索瑟（JD Souther）以及最成功的罗德斯坦在内的多位艺人。诚然，这在今天看起来有点中规中矩，这个音乐时代此后已被朋克和新浪潮所击溃，但阿什后来又与雪儿（Cher）、黛安娜·罗斯（Diana Ross）和10,000 Maniacs等具有信誉度的艺人合作，甚至还制作了男孩地带（Boyzone）和莫里西（Morrissey）的专辑。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在这场成就的游行中，阿什展现出一种令人印象深刻的镇定自若的形象，在许多方面谦逊低调，但也没有将自己的光芒藏在斗篷下。大牌合作者对他的感激之情显而易见，但他同时也为一些更为边缘的人物留出了空间，尤其是卡罗尔·金（Carole King）给人留下了深刻的印象。但最能引起共鸣的，或许还是与已故前搭档瓦勒的互动，阿什所设定的虚拟二重唱尤其令人感动。", "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "电影", "links": [{"text": "Film", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/film/film"}], article_text:
R ock’n’roll is notorious for its tales of bad behaviour: throwing TVs out of the window, mountains of cocaine, parades of groupies … but you won’t find any of that here. Peter Asher, brother of Jane, one half of Peter and Gordon, and super-successful producer of acts such as James Taylor and Linda Ronstadt, appears to be about as nerdish and clean-living as a 60s/70s music industry veteran could be. Although that might just be what he wants us to think; what are the chances Asher is a complete reprobate away from the camera, and is just brilliant at hiding it? That glasses and ruffled shirt front combo definitely reminds you of someone a tad more sleazy, even before Asher himself reminds you about it in the final credits.

Whatever the truth, Asher by any standards carved an amazing path, making the absolute most of being in the right place at the right time. Smartly structured around Asher’s anecdotes-and-music live show, the film stitches together a collection of clips, audio and musical performances that gallops through his personal backstory. His luckiest break, of course, was that his early partnership with schoolfriend Gordon Waller (modelled, it turned out, on the Everly Brothers) benefited from cast-off songs handed over by his sister’s boyfriend, one Paul McCartney; there’s an amusing moment where we hear John Lennon’s sneer at the lyric of what would become Peter and Gordon’s first and biggest hit, A World Without Love: “Please lock me away …” “Yes”. While the film clearly acknowledges the debt to McCartney’s songwriting (which presumably Lennon vetoed for the Beatles), it’s perhaps not quite ready to admit that without this connection, none of what followed would have happened at all.

At one point Asher says he wasn’t much of a pop star, and subsequent events suggest he was probably right. He appears to have been more comfortable away from the spotlight, thereby allowing him to become a ubiquitous figure in the Beatles’ orbit in swinging 60s London to which the title alludes. He was a co-owner of supercool art gallery Indica (where Lennon first met Yoko Ono), though given it only lasted two years, possibly he wasn’t all that great at that, either. It was the Beatles’ connection, though, that allowed him to really come into his own, when he was appointed head of A&R at the newly formed Apple Records, with his own top floor office in the Savile Row building.

Asher’s big discovery was Taylor, who had relocated to London after failing to get anywhere at home in the US; after producing Taylor’s debut album (which with characteristic modesty he says he messed up with Beatles-style orchestration), Asher followed Taylor to Los Angeles and settled into a quietly impressive second act as a producer and manager. After producing Taylor’s breakthrough second album, Sweet Baby James, Asher became a key figure in 1970s Californian soft rock, overseeing acts including Andrew Gold, Kate Taylor, JD Souther and – most successful of all – Ronstadt. Admittedly, this now looks a tad middle of the road, a musical era since vanquished by punk and new wave, but Asher later got on board with credibility-stoking artists such as Cher, Diana Ross and 10,000 Maniacs, and even produced albums by Boyzone and Morrissey.

Throughout this parade of achievement, Asher cuts an impressively self-possessed figure, unassuming in many ways but also not hiding his light under a bushel. The appreciation he gets from his big-name collaborators is clear enough, but he also gives houseroom to somewhat more tangential figures, with Carole King in particular coming across strongly. But it’s the interactions with late former partner Waller that are probably the most resonant, with the virtual duet Asher sets up being especially moving.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Cineverse has snagged VOD and streaming rights to Ralph’s Perfekt Christmas . The genre-bending feature stars Tom McLaren and counts former Twentieth Century Fox exec Mary McLaren among its producers.

It is the debut feature from Mary McLaren and Tom McLaren’s Next Chapter Entertainment banner. Cineverse has rights for North America and will release the film on-demand and on its Screambox streamer in Nov.

Per the synopsis, Tom McLaren ( Expelled ) stars as Ralph, a likable family man whose fanatical obsession with Christmas pushes his wife away. Determined to win her back, Ralph devises a crazy plan involving kidnapping the former child star of his favorite Christmas movie. Ralph’s pursuit of his perfect Christmas, however, takes dark and unexpected turns.

Related Stories

Cineverse Wins North American Rights To Thriller-Horror 'The Night Driver' With Josh Lucas, Alyssa Milano & David Arquette

Cineverse Acquires Genre-Bending Thriller 'Eugene The Marine' Starring Scott Glenn

The film also stars Charlie Schlatter ( Diagnosis: Murder ), Jill Schoelen ( The Stepfather ), Casey Burke ( The Middle ), Landon Gimenez ( Resurrection ) and Lynda Day George ( Roots ).

Watch on Deadline

Mary McLaren and Tom McLaren produced the film through their Next Chapter Entertainment banner. They served as supervising directors, with Matthew Bellamy as director of physical production. The screenplay was written by Jeremy Padow and Tom McLaren.

“ Ralph’s Perfekt Christmas is exactly the kind of smart, distinctive, genre-bending film that resonates with Cineverse and Screambox audiences,” said Dan Fisher, vice president of acquisitions at Cineverse. “The film combines an original story with unexpected twists, turns, and a surprise ending coupled with a standout performance by Tom McLaren as Ralph.”

“We set out to target everyone who considers Die Hard a ‘Christmas Movie’ and Cineverse is an ideal distribution partner for reaching that audience seeking alternate holiday content,” said Mary McLaren, who previously served as Chief Operating Officer, International Theatrical and Worldwide Home Entertainment, at Twentieth Century Fox.

We have the first look at the trailer.

article_text:
うるわしの宵の月

劇場公開日： 2026年10月23日

解説・あらすじ

講談社「デザート」連載のやまもり三香による人気少女漫画「うるわしの宵の月」を実写映画化した青春ラブストーリー。「今夜、世界からこの恋が消えても」の道枝駿佑が主演、「カラダ探し THE LAST NIGHT」の安斉星来がヒロインを務め、同じ高校でそれぞれ「王子」と呼ばれる男女が織りなす初恋の行方を描く。 高校1年生の少女・滝口宵は中性的な美しさとクールな振る舞いで「王子」と呼ばれているが、内心ではその完璧な王子像に複雑な思いを抱いていた。そんなある日、高校の先輩で同じく「王子」と呼ばれる完璧なルックスの男子生徒・市村琥珀と出会う。それぞれ自分の内面と周囲からのギャップに葛藤する2人は次第に惹かれ合い、“自分らしさ”と向き合いながら少しずつ距離を縮めていく。 琥珀と宵の関係を揺り動かす3人目の「王子」こと大路拓人役で水沢林太郎、琥珀の幼なじみ・よしこ役で与田祐希、宵の父・誠一役で藤木直人、琥珀と宵の恋の行方を見守る友人役で星乃夢奈、鈴川紗由、大倉空人、阿佐辰美が共演。「交換ウソ日記」の竹村謙太郎監督がメガホンをとり、「翔んで埼玉」「かぐや様は告らせたい 天才たちの恋愛頭脳戦」など数々のヒット作を手がけてきた徳永友一が脚本を担当。

2026年製作／119分／G／日本 配給：東宝 劇場公開日：2026年10月23日

"paragraph", "text": "这个新类别是2026年大奖的最重要进展。17年来，全景摄影奖一直在致敬全景画幅，而17年来参赛者也一直要求设立一个专门的航拍组。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "丹尼尔·维涅·加西亚凭借一组横跨安第斯山脉高地和阿根廷普纳高原的作品斩获公开组最高荣誉。他的获奖作品《沉睡的巨人》拍摄于智利的帕里纳科塔火山，该火山海拔超过6,300米，与其毗邻的波梅拉佩火山海拔超过6,200米。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": and Prashant Chacko）拍摄的《橄榄球运动员》荣获2026年爱普生数码艺术奖", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "来自西班牙的米克尔·伊拉埃塔（Mikel Iraeta）凭借《米尔福德峡湾的双重拱桥》（Double arch on Milford Sound）赢得公开组自然与风貌类别，他将这幅作品形容为几乎不可能完成的拍摄。“米尔福德峡湾是一个平均一年有300天下雨的地方，”伊拉埃塔说，“我去的前一天，通往那里的路因为有雪崩危险而关闭。要有一个完全晴朗的夜晚，没有雨、没有云、没有月亮，并且这一切恰好赶在9月底能够捕捉到银河双弧的时刻，这是非常困难的。最终的影像由107张不同的照片组合而成。”", "translated": true}, "来自意大利的弗朗西斯科·达尔奥尔莫（Francesco Dall’Olmo）在公开组航拍类别中凭借在罗弗敦群岛拍摄的《极光之翼》（Boreal Wings）获得第二名。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "来自泰国的武蒂梅·本亚西里西特（Wutimet true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "来自西班牙的托马斯·桑切斯·鲁伊斯（Tomás Sánchez Ruiz）夺得年度业余摄影师称号，并凭冰岛作品《斯托克斯尼斯双拱》（Double Arch Over Stokksnes）赢得业余自然与风景组冠军。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": Heaven）赢得业余建筑环境组冠军，并凭《球体》（Sphere）获得第二名，两幅作品均拍摄于巴伦西亚的艺术科学城。“我使用广角镜将八张照片合成一张，旨在让楼梯的优美曲线引导视线从地面延伸至天空，”他说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴西的马西奥·埃斯特维斯·卡布拉尔（Marcio Esteves "text": "荷兰的马克斯·特温特（Max Terwindt）凭在南极半岛拍摄的《南极之夜》（Antarctic Nights）获得策展人奖（The Curator’s Award。“那是我第一次去那里，整个经历真的非常神奇，”特温特说，“我们获得了飞无人机的特别许可。由于南极的夏天从不天黑，日落慢慢淡入日出，所以它从黄金时刻过渡到蓝色时刻，又回到了黄金时刻。”", "translated": 行星奖（RAW Planet Award）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "爱普生全景大奖赛创始人兼策展人戴维·埃文斯（David true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "爱普生国际全景大奖赛是全球最大的全景摄影专注赛事，爱普生澳大利亚公司与爱普生东南亚公司共同担任主要赞助商。其声誉建立在一个对摄影师提出比几乎任何其他赛事都更高要求的格式之上。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": In addition to their creativity, these entries must show excellence in digital post-processing as well as exceptional photographic technique."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The Rugby Players, winner of The Epson Digital Art Prize 2026, shot by Preeti and Prashant Chacko"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The winner of The Epson Digital Art Prize 2026 was The Rugby Players shot by Preeti and Prashant Chacko (who entered as a couple from India) and who commented on their stunning image saying, “Southern white rhinos are, in their normal state, surprisingly unthreatening – calm grazers who move around at a leisurely pace. One morning at Solio Game Reserve in Kenya we were photographing a group of eight rhinos with a few cattle egrets walking among them, a rare sighting in most other national parks. Something suddenly shifted and five of the rhinos broke into a run. We understood in that instant why a group of rhinos is called a crash. Neither of us has ever played rugby, but from the point of view of the egrets this is how we imagine a forward pack must look, heads down and all that weight already committed.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Mikel Iraeta of Spain won the Open Nature and Landscape category with Double arch on Milford Sound, an image he describes as close to impossible to make. “Milford Sound is a place where it rains on average 300 days a year,” Iraeta said. “The day before I visited, the access road was closed due to snow avalanche danger. It is very difficult to have an entire clear night with no rain, no clouds, no moon and for all of this to coincide at the end of September when it is possible to capture the double arc of the Milky Way. The final image is the result of combining 107 different photographs.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Xuecheng Liu of the United States won the Open Built Environment category with Center of the Cosmos, a stitched panorama of Times Square from above. “Times Square is one of the most photographed places in the world, so my challenge was to find a perspective that could make such a familiar place feel unfamiliar again,” Liu said. “I stitched together 25 frames to create an ultra-wide aerial panorama, with countless points of light resembling stars surrounding the centre of a galaxy.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Francesco Dall’Olmo of Italy placed second in Open Aerial with Boreal Wings, photographed in the Lofoten Islands."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Wutimet Bunyasirisith of Thailand was named Southeast Asia Open Photographer of the Year for The Emerald Arch Over Lofoten, made at Skagsanden Beach in Norway."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“The Northern Lights flared up and curved perfectly around the mountain,” Bunyasirisith said. “The display was so vastly immense that even my 12mm ultra-wide lens couldn’t capture the entire scene in a single frame. My only choice was to shoot a panorama. The conditions that night were brutal, freezing cold, biting winds and I had to wade into the icy seawater to get the shot.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Hattori Tai, Regional Director of Commercial and Industrial Inkjet Products, Epson Southeast Asia said: “We are thrilled to celebrate the exceptional talent emerging from Southeast Asia for the third year running. Wutimet’s success reflects a continuing trend of Southeast Asian photographers venturing to distant global landscapes to capture back awe-inspiring, world-class panoramic visuals. His work has shown us relentless passion, vision and technical discipline that define our region’s creative community. Epson is honoured to support our region’s best visual storytellers with world-class print solutions that preserve the depth, scale and rich colour of their photography.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Tomás Sánchez Ruiz of Spain claimed the Amateur Photographer of the Year title, winning the Amateur Nature and Landscape category with Double Arch Over Stokksnes in Iceland."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“On the night I took this photograph, the aurora forecast was not particularly promising,” Sánchez Ruiz said. “When I pulled back the curtain of our hotel room and saw a green glow in the sky, I knew this could be the night we had been waiting for. The black sand was completely covered in freshly fallen, untouched snow. And there I was, finally taking the photograph I had been waiting for, with a smile on my face.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "His Amateur Built Environment entry, Westminster Abbey, was also recognised. “As soon as I entered the chapel and saw its enormous stained-glass windows, the spectacular ribs of the vaulted ceiling and the flags lining both sides of the room, I knew I had to get my camera out,” he said."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In the Amateur Aerial category, Xuejun Long of China won with Journey of Life, made at Lake Magadi in Kenya. “As the freshwater evaporated, chemical deposits on the lakebed were exposed, forming lots of interconnected patterns,” Long said. “I was lucky to catch this moment and a flock of flamingos flew in, adding life and bringing a dreamy, magical scene from the sky.” Mildred Lai of Hong Kong placed second with The Devil’s Gaze."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Sebastián Cantos Navalon of Spain won Amateur Built Environment with Stairs from Earth to Heaven and placed second with Sphere, both photographed at the City of Arts and Sciences in Valencia. “I used a wide-angle lens and created a composite image from eight shots, aiming for the curved lines of the staircase to guide the eye from the ground towards the sky,” he said."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Marcio Esteves Cabral of Brazil was named VR/360 Photographer of the Year for Diving in a blue dream, made at Cenote El Edén in Mexico, with Luis García Márquez of Spain placing second with Harvest of Light."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Max Terwindt of The Netherlands received The Curator’s Award for Antarctic Nights, made on the Antarctic Peninsula. “It was my first time there and the whole experience was truly magical,” Terwindt said. “We had a special license to fly our drones. As it never becomes dark in the Antarctic summer, the sunset slowly faded into the sunrise, so it went from golden hour to blue hour to golden hour again.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Szabi Nemeth of Australia took Highest Scoring Vertical Image with Between Giants, photographed in the Indian Ocean off Mauritius, and Vitaly Golovatyuk took Highest Scoring Gigapixel Image with X marks the spot in Shanghai. Garcia also collected the RAW Planet Award."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“In the 17-year history of The Epson Pano Awards, never has a request from entrants been stronger than the addition of a dedicated Aerial category,” said Pano Awards founder and curator David Evans. “The addition of a new Aerial category this year in both the Open and Amateur competitions was therefore expectedly popular, with some 680 Aerial entries. The aerial perspective opens up so much of the world above tripod level and the panoramic format lends itself beautifully to this way of seeing. I look forward to watching how this category will evolve over coming years, as technology enables photographers to push their own boundaries and limits.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The Epson International Pano Awards is the world’s largest competition dedicated to panoramic photography and Epson Australia is the main sponsor alongside Epson Southeast Asia. Its reputation rests on a format that demands more from a photographer than almost any other."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "To view the full gallery of 2026 winning and runner-up images go to: https://thepanoawards.com", "links": [{"text": "https://thepanoawards.com", "url": "https://thepanoawards.com"}]}]
article_text:
The 17th Epson International Pano Awards has announced its 2026 winners, with Spanish photographer Daniel Viñé Garcia named Open Photographer of the Year and Tomás Sánchez Ruiz , also of Spain, taking Amateur Photographer of the Year.

Open Photographer of the Year Daniel Viñé Garcia’s The Sleeping Giant

This year’s competition drew 4,084 entries from photographers in 93 countries, an increase of 19 percent on 2025. Entries divided into 2,122 in the Open competition and 1,962 in the Amateur competition, with the field including 680 entries in the new Aerial categories.

“Photographers at every level, from first-time entrants to established professionals, use the Pano Awards as a benchmark for their own work,” said Craig Heckenberg, Managing Director of Epson Australia and New Zealand. “The aerial category is a perfect example of why the competition has stayed relevant for 17 years. It responds to what photographers are actually doing and it gives the global industry a view of where the craft is heading next.”

That new category is the headline development of the 2026 awards. For 17 years the Pano Awards has celebrated the panoramic format and for 17 years entrants have asked for a dedicated aerial division.

Daniel Viñé Garcia took the top Open honour on the strength of a portfolio that spans the high Andes and the Argentine Puna. His winning image, The Sleeping Giant, was made at Parinacota Volcano in Chile, rising more than 6,300 metres and paired with the neighbouring Pomerape at over 6,200 metres.

“The original capture was a 360-degree aerial panorama made from 33 individual exposures,” Garcia said. “After one last burst of light, the landscape gradually took on magenta tones, wrapping the volcanoes and the high-altitude lakes in a particularly special atmosphere. I later refined the framing from the full panorama to concentrate the final composition on the volcanoes, the light and the shapes of the landscape.”

His work also earned places in the Open Nature and Landscape category with Cathedral of Starlight, a night panorama made at around 3,100 metres in the Argentine Puna and My Perfect Night, photographed on a salt flat in Catamarca at more than 3,300 metres.

Other key awards include The Epson Digital Art Prize, which is decided by the executive team at Epson Australia from the top 50 entries in each category of the Open competition. In addition to their creativity, these entries must show excellence in digital post-processing as well as exceptional photographic technique.

The Rugby Players, winner of The Epson Digital Art Prize 2026, shot by Preeti and Prashant Chacko

The winner of The Epson Digital Art Prize 2026 was The Rugby Players shot by Preeti and Prashant Chacko (who entered as a couple from India) and who commented on their stunning image saying, “Southern white rhinos are, in their normal state, surprisingly unthreatening – calm grazers who move around at a leisurely pace. One morning at Solio Game Reserve in Kenya we were photographing a group of eight rhinos with a few cattle egrets walking among them, a rare sighting in most other national parks. Something suddenly shifted and five of the rhinos broke into a run. We understood in that instant why a group of rhinos is called a crash. Neither of us has ever played rugby, but from the point of view of the egrets this is how we imagine a forward pack must look, heads down and all that weight already committed.”

Mikel Iraeta of Spain won the Open Nature and Landscape category with Double arch on Milford Sound, an image he describes as close to impossible to make. “Milford Sound is a place where it rains on average 300 days a year,” Iraeta said. “The day before I visited, the access road was closed due to snow avalanche danger. It is very difficult to have an entire clear night with no rain, no clouds, no moon and for all of this to coincide at the end of September when it is possible to capture the double arc of the Milky Way. The final image is the result of combining 107 different photographs.”

Xuecheng Liu of the United States won the Open Built Environment category with Center of the Cosmos, a stitched panorama of Times Square from above. “Times Square is one of the most photographed places in the world, so my challenge was to find a perspective that could make such a familiar place feel unfamiliar again,” Liu said. “I stitched together 25 frames to create an ultra-wide aerial panorama, with countless points of light resembling stars surrounding the centre of a galaxy.”

Francesco Dall’Olmo of Italy placed second in Open Aerial with Boreal Wings, photographed in the Lofoten Islands.

Wutimet Bunyasirisith of Thailand was named Southeast Asia Open Photographer of the Year for The Emerald Arch Over Lofoten, made at Skagsanden Beach in Norway.

“The Northern Lights flared up and curved perfectly around the mountain,” Bunyasirisith said. “The display was so vastly immense that even my 12mm ultra-wide lens couldn’t capture the entire scene in a single frame. My only choice was to shoot a panorama. The conditions that night were brutal, freezing cold, biting winds and I had to wade into the icy seawater to get the shot.”

Hattori Tai, Regional Director of Commercial and Industrial Inkjet Products, Epson Southeast Asia said: “We are thrilled to celebrate the exceptional talent emerging from Southeast Asia for the third year running. Wutimet’s success reflects a continuing trend of Southeast Asian photographers venturing to distant global landscapes to capture back awe-inspiring, world-class panoramic visuals. His work has shown us relentless passion, vision and technical discipline that define our region’s creative community. Epson is honoured to support our region’s best visual storytellers with world-class print solutions that preserve the depth, scale and rich colour of their photography.”

Tomás Sánchez Ruiz of Spain claimed the Amateur Photographer of the Year title, winning the Amateur Nature and Landscape category with Double Arch Over Stokksnes in Iceland.

“On the night I took this photograph, the aurora forecast was not particularly promising,” Sánchez Ruiz said. “When I pulled back the curtain of our hotel room and saw a green glow in the sky, I knew this could be the night we had been waiting for. The black sand was completely covered in freshly fallen, untouched snow. And there I was, finally taking the photograph I had been waiting for, with a smile on my face.”

His Amateur Built Environment entry, Westminster Abbey, was also recognised. “As soon as I entered the chapel and saw its enormous stained-glass windows, the spectacular ribs of the vaulted ceiling and the flags lining both sides of the room, I knew I had to get my camera out,” he said.

In the Amateur Aerial category, Xuejun Long of China won with Journey of Life, made at Lake Magadi in Kenya. “As the freshwater evaporated, chemical deposits on the lakebed were exposed, forming lots of interconnected patterns,” Long said. “I was lucky to catch this moment and a flock of flamingos flew in, adding life and bringing a dreamy, magical scene from the sky.” Mildred Lai of Hong Kong placed second with The Devil’s Gaze.

Sebastián Cantos Navalon of Spain won Amateur Built Environment with Stairs from Earth to Heaven and placed second with Sphere, both photographed at the City of Arts and Sciences in Valencia. “I used a wide-angle lens and created a composite image from eight shots, aiming for the curved lines of the staircase to guide the eye from the ground towards the sky,” he said.

Marcio Esteves Cabral of Brazil was named VR/360 Photographer of the Year for Diving in a blue dream, made at Cenote El Edén in Mexico, with Luis García Márquez of Spain placing second with Harvest of Light.

Max Terwindt of The Netherlands received The Curator’s Award for Antarctic Nights, made on the Antarctic Peninsula. “It was my first time there and the whole experience was truly magical,” Terwindt said. “We had a special license to fly our drones. As it never becomes dark in the Antarctic summer, the sunset slowly faded into the sunrise, so it went from golden hour to blue hour to golden hour again.”

Szabi Nemeth of Australia took Highest Scoring Vertical Image with Between Giants, photographed in the Indian Ocean off Mauritius, and Vitaly Golovatyuk took Highest Scoring Gigapixel Image with X marks the spot in Shanghai. Garcia also collected the RAW Planet Award.

“In the 17-year history of The Epson Pano Awards, never has a request from entrants been stronger than the addition of a dedicated Aerial category,” said Pano Awards founder and curator David Evans. “The addition of a new Aerial category this year in both the Open and Amateur competitions was therefore expectedly popular, with some 680 Aerial entries. The aerial perspective opens up so much of the world above tripod level and the panoramic format lends itself beautifully to this way of seeing. I look forward to watching how this category will evolve over coming years, as technology enables photographers to push their own boundaries and limits.”

The Epson International Pano Awards is the world’s largest competition dedicated to panoramic photography and Epson Australia is the main sponsor alongside Epson Southeast Asia. Its reputation rests on a format that demands more from a photographer than almost any other.

To view the full gallery of 2026 winning and runner-up images go to: https://thepanoawards.com

editorial_excerpt_zh: 注：本篇影评最初作为我们2026年多伦多国际电影节（TIFF）报道的一部分发表。该片将于10月23日在院线上映。正如TIFF这样的电影节需要世界首映一样，老牌女演员也需要电影。本片《谋杀天赋》便是如此，它属于一种被称为……的次类型
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "注：本篇影评最初作为我们2026年多伦多国际电影节（TIFF）报道的一部分发表。该片将于10月23日在院线上映。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "正如TIFF这样的电影节需要世界首映一样，老牌女演员也需要电影。本片《谋杀天赋》便是如此，它属于一种被称为“Mirrenslop”的次类型。其他亮点（或者说槽点）包括以色列传记片《果尔达》，与那部电影一样，本片或许能为发行商赢得一个象征性的奥斯卡最佳化妆奖提名。有鉴于此，海伦·米伦（Mirren）经过一番化妆，饰演了美国最伟大的作家之一帕特里夏·海史密斯（Patricia Highsmith）。这位作家以无可争议的杰作《天才雷普利》最为知名，她曾通过犯罪小说来探索仿佛涵盖全人类的经验。对于这部对其在世最后一年进行高度虚构化的作品，她会赞同吗？多半不会。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "1995年，出版公司员工爱德华（奥尔登·埃伦瑞奇饰）被派往瑞士，去说服海史密斯（米伦饰）写最后一部雷普利小说。这位日渐衰老、嗜酒如命且脾气暴躁的海史密斯远没有被说服。不过，爱德华对她作品的了解以及坚持不懈地帮她构思一个点子，最终还是赢得了她的芳心。或者更准确地说：当他向她敞开心扉，谈及自己、艰辛的童年、死去的父母，甚至是他在去那里的火车上遇到的那个富家漂亮女孩（奥莉薇亚·库克饰）时，她意识到这里有着创作完美谋杀故事的素材。比如，如果爱德华想要融入火车上那个女孩的富有家庭会怎样？自此，现实与虚构开始交织，尽管这种交织从未达到令人眼花缭乱或引发深思的程度。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "将一个十分愚蠢的概念相对严肃地呈现出来，《谋杀天赋》在可看之余也相当套路。导演安东·寇班（Anton Corbijn）曾是Joy Division和U2乐队的摄影师，后来转型为电影人，他曾经看起来是一位很有前途的导演，但近来似乎满足于拍出水准过得去的粗制滥造之作。对一部未完成的雷普利小说的戏剧化处理发生风景秀丽的瑞士取景地，让人想起他此前对淡化版梅尔维尔作品《美国人》的翻拍，尽管离那部电影刻意经营的艺术片节奏还有相当距离。我想人们不得不为他放弃任何矫饰而鼓掌。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "通过片中至少有三次海史密斯突然从虚空中现身的惊吓桥段，你大概就能看出寇班在涉足什么领域了。同样，她不断抛出注定能轻松博得观众一笑的俏皮话。在米伦（固然算不上无聊）略显敷衍的表演中，埃伦瑞奇的角色凸显出他那张紧绷而英俊的面孔如何稳稳地兼具了讨人喜欢的男主角与邪恶杀手的特质。你会想起2009年他在弗朗西斯·福特·科波拉的《泰特罗》中崭露头角时，为何会赢得“杰克·尼科尔森”式的比较。只可惜到头来，这两人之间的化学反应显得如此肤浅。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "无论如何，《谋杀天赋》堪称合格的平庸之作的定义。然而，海史密斯的全部作品——通过对厌女症、阶级以及每个人不可知特质的尖锐探讨，竭力超越早期同类“机场”小说的作品——却绝非如此。她理应得到比针对特定院线的凑数填充物更好的待遇。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《谋杀天赋》于2026年多伦多国际电影节首映，并于10月23日上映。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Note: This review was originally published as part of our 2026 TIFF coverage. The film opens in theaters on October 23 ."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Old ladies need movies as festivals like TIFF need world premieres. So is the case with A Talent for Murder , which can be applied to a subgenre known as Mirrenslop. Other highlights (or rather lowlights) include the Israeli hagiography Golda and, like that film, this may get a distributor its one token Oscar nomination in the makeup category. As such, Mirren is done up to play one of America’s greatest writers, Patricia Highsmith. Best known for The Talented Mr. Ripley , an undeniable masterpiece, the author used crime fiction to explore what feels like all of human experience. Would she approve of this heavily fictionalized account of her last year on earth? Likely not."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In 1995, publishing-house employee Edward (Alden Ehrenreich) is sent to Switzerland to convince Highsmith (Mirren) to write one last Ripley book. The aging, heavy-drinking, curmudgeonly Highsmith is far from convinced. Edward’s knowledge of her work and persistence in at least helping her craft an idea eventually win her over, though. Or rather: when he opens up to her about himself, his hardscrabble childhood, dead parents, and even the pretty rich girl (Olivia Cooke) he met on the train there, she realizes there’s material for a perfect murder story. What if Edward, for example, wanted to integrate himself into that girl on the train’s rich family? From here, fact and fiction begin to blend, though never in any way too disorienting or thought-provoking."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Taking a very silly concept and playing it relatively straight, A Talent for Murder is fairly predictable, if watchable. The helmer, Joy Division and U2 photographer-turned-filmmaker Anton Corbijn, once seemed a promising director, but as of late appears content with nice-enough-looking hackwork. The dramatizations of an unwritten Ripley novel are set in nice Swiss locations, recalling his work on the watered-down Melville riff The American , if quite far from that film’s deliberate arthouse pacing. I guess one has to applaud him for giving up any pretensions."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "You’ll probably know what territory Corbijn is treading by the fact that there are at least three jump scares involving Highsmith appearing out of nowhere. Likewise, she’s constantly spouting one-liners sure to get the audience’s easy-laughers. article_text:
Note: This review was originally published as part of our 2026 TIFF coverage. The film opens in theaters on October 23 .

Old ladies need movies as festivals like TIFF need world premieres. So is the case with A Talent for Murder , which can be applied to a subgenre known as Mirrenslop. Other highlights (or rather lowlights) include the Israeli hagiography Golda and, like that film, this may get a distributor its one token Oscar nomination in the makeup category. As such, Mirren is done up to play one of America’s greatest writers, Patricia Highsmith. Best known for The Talented Mr. Ripley , an undeniable masterpiece, the author used crime fiction to explore what feels like all of human experience. Would she approve of this heavily fictionalized account of her last year on earth? Likely not.

In 1995, publishing-house employee Edward (Alden Ehrenreich) is sent to Switzerland to convince Highsmith (Mirren) to write one last Ripley book. The aging, heavy-drinking, curmudgeonly Highsmith is far from convinced. Edward’s knowledge of her work and persistence in at least helping her craft an idea eventually win her over, though. Or rather: when he opens up to her about himself, his hardscrabble childhood, dead parents, and even the pretty rich girl (Olivia Cooke) he met on the train there, she realizes there’s material for a perfect murder story. What if Edward, for example, wanted to integrate himself into that girl on the train’s rich family? From here, fact and fiction begin to blend, though never in any way too disorienting or thought-provoking.

Taking a very silly concept and playing it relatively straight, A Talent for Murder is fairly predictable, if watchable. The helmer, Joy Division and U2 photographer-turned-filmmaker Anton Corbijn, once seemed a promising director, but as of late appears content with nice-enough-looking hackwork. The dramatizations of an unwritten Ripley novel are set in nice Swiss locations, recalling his work on the watered-down Melville riff The American , if quite far from that film’s deliberate arthouse pacing. I guess one has to applaud him for giving up any pretensions.

You’ll probably know what territory Corbijn is treading by the fact that there are at least three jump scares involving Highsmith appearing out of nowhere. Likewise, she’s constantly spouting one-liners sure to get the audience’s easy-laughers. Amidst Mirren’s (admittedly not-boring) glazed ham acting, Ehrenreich’s role emphasizes just how steadily his scrunched, handsome face contains both a likable leading man and sinister killer. You remember why he was earning comparisons to Jack Nicholson when he appeared on the scene with Francis Ford Coppola’s Tetro in 2009. It’s just a shame the dynamic between these two feels so shallow at the end of the day.

For whatever it’s worth, A Talent for Murder is the definition of a competent mediocrity. Yet Highsmith’s oeuvre—which did everything to transcend the early equivalent of “airport” novels through searing explorations of misogyny, class, and the unknowable quality of every person—was anything but. She deserves better than specialty-box-office filler.

A Talent for Murder premiered at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival and opens on October 23.

article_text:
Oscilloscope Laboratories has acquired U.S. rights to the psychosexual thriller “ Act One ” from writer-director Sophia Takal (“Always Shine,” “Black Christmas”), and will release it in theaters in 2027.

“Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story” star Ella Beatty will play the leading role of Hannah, a sheltered seventeen-year-old aspiring actress. “Act One” follows Hannah as she joins an elite acting studio led by its magnetic founder, Melanie (Ari Graynor). Per the press release, “Drawn to Melanie’s intensity and increasingly extreme methods, Hannah throws herself into the work. But as dedication turns to obsession and the lines between performance, desire and manipulation blur, she is pulled into a dangerous game that tests how far she’ll go to become the artist she wants to be.”

Related Stories

Cannes Chief Thierry Fremaux Hails French Film Model as CNC Head Gaëtan Bruel Vows to Fight for Its Future at 80th Anniversary

Joel Coen Teases Reunion Film With Brother Ethan: There Are ‘Other Stories That We’ve Thought About’

The film also stars Sinclair Daniel (“Insidious: The Red Door”), Tavi Gevinson (“Gossip Girl”), Elizabeth Reaser (“Twilight”), Nate Mann (“Masters of the Air”) and Robert Sean Leonard (“House”).

“I’m thrilled Oscilloscope is releasing ‘Act One,’” Takal said. “Getting to work with them again after ‘Always Shine’ feels like a homecoming. It’s heartening to know there are people out there with the taste, nerve and good sense to champion movies like ours. I can’t wait for audiences to see the incredible work of all the talented people who made this film!”

The film debuted at Tribeca Festival on June 10. “Act One” is produced by Takal, Allison Rose Carter (Savage Rose Films), Julie Christeas (Tandem Pictures), Jon Read (Savage Rose Films), Stephanie Roush (Foxglove Films), and Julie Waters (Watermark Media). Executive producers are Evan Dyal of Watermark Media, Ryan Kampe of Visit Films, Lawrence Michael Levine, Allison and Jon Stockel and Marilyn White.

"正如约翰逊所说“我希望他们不是作为模特，而是作为朋友出镜”，此次广告大片比起罗列明星，更聚焦于品牌与人之间的关系。长期以来从亲密距离持续拍摄朋友、爱人与艺术家私生活的戈尔丁的照片，以及重视与社群对话的 Acne Studios。这成为了两者的态度相互重合的项目。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
アクネ ストゥディオズが、ブランド創立30周年を記念したキャンペーンを発表した。撮影を手がけたのは、アメリカを代表する写真家ナン・ゴールディン。ブランドの原点である「デニム」をテーマに、これまでアクネ ストゥディオズと関係を築いてきたクリエイターたちをポートレートに収めている。

アクネ ストゥディオズの歴史は1996年、ストックホルムで制作された100本のローデニムジーンズから始まった。「Ambition to Create Novel Expressions（新しい表現を創造する野望）」の頭文字を取った「Acne」として活動を開始し、ジーンズを地元のアーティストやクリエイター、友人たちへ贈ったことがブランドの出発点だった。2006年に現在の名称へ変更し、ファッション、アート、カルチャーを横断するブランドへと発展してきた。

30周年を迎え、共同創設者兼クリエイティブ・ディレクターのジョニー・ヨハンソンが改めて目を向けたのが、その原点であるデニム。ブランドにとって初のコラボレーションとなるゴールディンは、過去30年間を象徴するデニムの現行モデルやアーカイブ、復刻モデルをまとった人々を、親密かつダイレクトなポートレートとして撮影した。

被写体となったのは、ミュージシャンのエリー・ロウゼル、モデル兼写真家のグィネヴィア・ヴァン・シーナス、アーティストのジョナサン・リンドン・チェイス、写真家ジョーダン・ヘミングウェイ、俳優兼ミュージシャンのジュリエット・ルイス、アーティストのピーター・シュレシンジャー、俳優兼モデルのラヤ・マルティニー、俳優の福島リラ、アーティストのサンドラ・ポールソンら。いずれも過去のコラボレーションや対話を通して、ブランドの現在を形づくってきた人物たちだ。

「モデルとしてではなく、友人として出演してもらいたかった」とヨハンソンが語るように、今回のキャンペーンはスターを並べることよりも、ブランドと人との関係性に焦点を当てている。長年、友人や恋人、アーティストたちの私生活を親密な距離から撮り続けてきたゴールディンの写真と、コミュニティとの対話を重視してきたアクネ ストゥディオズ。その両者の姿勢が重なり合うプロジェクトとなった。

article_text:
Museum Unions

V&A Museum Staff Set to Strike Across All Four London Sites

Allegations of “Amazon-style” working conditions and calls for pay raises prompted unionized workers to authorize yet another strike at the UK museum network.

Editor's note 10/26/26 10:29 ET : As of Monday, October 26, both Prospect Union and Public and Commercial Services (PCS) Union have confirmed with Hyperallergic that they're suspending this week's forthcoming strike in light of an “improved offer” from the museum. Further negotiations are set to take place.

As negotiations continue at the Victoria & Albert Museum (V&A), unionized staff have publicized their intent to strike across all four London sites on October 29 and 30, citing continued disputes regarding pay and working conditions. The escalation comes after two strike actions at specific locations at the beginning and end of September.

Born from accusations of “Amazon-style” working conditions at the newly opened V&A East Storehouse — namely the alleged lack of sufficient breaks for hydration and restroom use — staff organized under Prospect Union’s heritage division and the Public and Commercial Services Union (PCS) voted overwhelmingly in favor of strike action this summer.

“Prospect members are dedicated to their jobs, and it is these dedicated staff who make the museum the world-class attraction it is,” said Prospect Union's general secretary, Mike Clancy, in a press statement. Clancy also accused V&A Director Tristram Hunt of refusing to participate in negotiations with the unions, “show[ing] the level of disdain in which he holds his staff.”

Both unions are also seeking minimum pay increases of 4% across the board, as well as an additional bump to bring the minimum hourly wage for the lowest-paid staff to £14.80 (~$20), which would make the V&A a Real London Living Wage accredited employer.

article_text:
Former UTA film agent Dante DeSario and media investor Michael Lambert have launched Collage , a management company devoted to AI -native production.

The new firm has closed a seed funding round, with Black Bear and Fundamental Films investing. Other investors and senior advisors include Dennis Miller, Blue Deer Media, GOAL Ventures, AGC Studios, Roy Lee, Marty Bowen, Todd Lieberman, Todd Garner, Barry Porter, George Huber, Max Michael, and Ric Roman Waugh.

Clients of the L.A.-based company at launch include a number of top-shelf names in the emerging arena of AI. On the roster are Asteria, the studio behind software platform Continuum and recent festival feature selections like Alpha Gang and Chikaboom! ; real-time 3D animation studio Defect; Berlin-based AI studio Lipstick; Matriarch, the AI-native and hybrid production company from ex-Luma Dream Lab L.A. chief Verena Puhm; Native Foreign, creator of the OpenAI-backed franchise Critterz ; Obsidian, Wes Walker’s studio partnership with Imagine Entertainment; Secret Level, the studio behind hybrid horror feature Terrarium ; and Lux Meridian, the generative production arm of Territory Group whose work includes Dune , The Martian , and Guardians of the Galaxy .

Related Stories

'Wildwood' Director Hopes People "See The Danger" In GenAI, Calls It "Antithetical" To Laika's Work

Stage 32 Launches Marketplace To Combat AI Slop

The stated goal of Collage is to build a bridge between AI-native production companies and Hollywood studios, streamers, filmmakers, and brands. Once connected, the company’s thesis holds, the parties will build their respective businesses, expand their reach, and develop commercial relationships.

Watch on Deadline

After a couple of years of high anxiety over how the influx of AI could reshape the production process and possibly eliminate jobs, the entertainment business has generally settled into a more pragmatic phase. On a macro level, the AI boom is contiuning apace, and against that backdrop a growing number of traditional players have been reaching across the aisle to Silicon Valley.

As a member of UTA’s independent film group, DeSario worked with filmmakers and packaged and arranged financing for hundreds of films, including Jordan Firstman’s Club Kid . The well-received Cannes title fetched a UTA-record in the high-teens millions in a sale to A24. Other films in DeSario’s portfolio included Damian McCarthy’s Hokum (Neon), Jennifer Peedom’s Tenzing (Apple), and Alex Ullom’s upcoming 4 x 4 (Neon).

Collage’s role in the emerging ecosystem of AI will be to help organize it by identifying top suppliers; matching production methods to projects; pricing and sizing projects; and helping to ensure proper management of the quality, legal and delivery aspects of production. The company will also invest selectively in companies, either directly or down the line through dedicated investment vehicles managed by Collage Capital.

“We saw extraordinary creative companies emerging around generative production, but very little infrastructure around them,” DeSario said in a statement. “Hollywood needed a trusted way to find and work with the best of these companies, while the companies themselves needed help with business development and operations, technology relationships, and capital. We built Collage to connect the two and give great creative companies the support they need to grow.”

article_text:
Top galleries are placing plenty of works for prices above $1 million at Art Basel Paris 2026 . Dealer Emmanuel Di Donna told ARTnews at the Avant-Première preview on Tuesday afternoon (aka the VVIP opening) that the experience is like “drinking from a fire hose.” That was followed by the VIP preview on Wednesday.

This all came off without a hitch amid heightened security as protests roiled Paris after demonstrations by high school students against crumbling educational infrastructure and absent teachers in a local suburb literally caught fire, with thousands taking to the streets, with some resulting property damage.

The priciest work on display, on offer from Pace Di Donna Schrader Galleries, is a rare 1917 painting of a reclining nude woman by Amedeo Modigliani, Nu étendu (Lolotte) , valued in excess of $100 million. As of Wednesday evening local time, there was no word on whether the piece had found a buyer, but its presence testified to dealers’ faith that top collectors would be in attendance despite the uproar in the streets.

“This opening afternoon has been very strong and collectors came ready to make decisions quickly,” said dealer Thaddaeus Ropac in an emailed statement. “Despite any worries about the demonstrations, some deciding not to travel to Paris, we already feel that it’s the most international art fair of the year.”

The fair came on the heels of Frieze and Frieze Masters, the contemporary art and 20th-century art fairs that took place in London last week. Hauser & Wirth president Marc Payot said in an emailed statement, “In the past 24 hours, we’ve sold super-rare works by Fontana, Gauguin, Modigliani and Morandi that we first introduced at Frieze. And in Paris, we are placing equally exceptional works on our stand—true masterpieces of the second half of the 20th century by Richter, Calder, Bourgeois, Twombly, Baselitz and Szapocznikow, along with new works by George Condo, Jenny Holzer, Henry Taylor, and Camille Henrot.”

Here’s every sale that has been reported as of 9 p.m. Paris time for $1 million and up.

The top prices were commanded by Hauser & Wirth, which sold Gerhard Richter’s 1965 work Rokokotisch (Rococo Table) and Georg Baselitz’s 1965 Der Hirte (The Shepherd) , each for a price in the region of $10 million.

David Zwirner sold a Gerhard Richter painting for $8.5 million.

White Cube sold Julie Mehretu’s 2001 painting Rise of the New Suprematists and her 2018 painting Mumbaphilia (J.E.) for $7.9 million each.

Pace sold Jean Dubuffet’s painting La chaise (1964) for a price over $5 million.

Zwirner sold Robert Ryman paintings for $4 million and $1.3 million.

Hauser & Wirth sold a Mark Bradford for $4 million.

Zwirner sold a 1957 Joan Mitchell painting for $3.8 million.

Zwirner sold a new Marlene Dumas painting for $3 million.

Zwirner placed a Josef Albers painting for $3 million.

Hauser & Wirth found a home for George Condo’s Woman with Designer Shirt (2026) for $2.95 million.

Zwirner sold a Luc Tuymans painting for $2.4 million.

Le Minotaure sold an untitled 1922 Wassily Kandinsky watercolor for $2.2 million.

Sprüth Magers sold George Condo’s painting The Mechanical Man (2026) to a US collection for $2.2 million. The gallery sold his painting Coney Island (2026) to a European collection for the same price.

Zwirner found a new home for an On Kawara painting for $2 million.

Pace sold Lee Ufan’s From Line No. 79061 (1979) for $2 million.

White Cube sold an El Anatsui sculpture, MivEvi I (2025), for $2 million.

Thaddaeus Ropac placed Lucio Fontana’s Concetto spaziale (1953), a painting with Murano glass fragments, for $2 million.

Hauser & Wirth sold Lucio Fontana’s 1961 work Concetto spaziale (Spatial Concept) for $1.9 million.

Gladstone sold Cecily Brown’s painting This must be the place (2017–21) for $1.5 million.

Hauser & Wirth sold Philip Guston’s Untitled (1969) for $1.5 million.

Gladstone sold Victor Man’s painting Pink Chair (2012) for $1.3 million.

White Cube sold Tracey Emin’s painting You Were Part of me (2022) for $1.3 million.

Zwirner sold a sculpture by Ruth Asawa for $1.2 million.

Georges-Philippe et Nathalie Vallois sold Niki de Saint Phalle’s multimedium sculpture Cat Head Totem (2000) for a price between $800,000 and $1.2 million.

Hauser & Wirth sold Henry Taylor’s painting “WTF’s my 40 acres & my mule, you lying…” (2023–26) for $1 million.

Lisson Gallery sold Anish Kapoor’s sculpture Clear to Dark Brandy (2026) for $1 million.

Mennour sold Lee Ufan’s Response (2026) for $1 million.

真実と反逆 ナチスと闘った若きレジスタンス

劇場公開日： 2026年10月16日

解説・あらすじ

第2次世界大戦下のドイツを舞台に、ナチスの真実を伝えるべく立ち上がった若きレジスタンスの命をかけた闘いを描いたヒューマンドラマ。ナチス政権下のドイツで反逆罪で処刑された実在の最年少レジスタンス、ヘルムス・ヒューブナーを題材に、「国家の圧力」と「自らの信念」との激しい衝突を描き出す。 1941年、第2次世界大戦下のドイツ。16歳の少年ヘルムス・ヒューブナーは、教会でナチス政権への服従を促され、ヒトラーの圧政に疑問を抱くようになる。ユダヤ人の迫害を目の当たりにしたことをきっかけに、禁止されていた海外のラジオ放送を聴いた彼は、国家が隠し続けてきた戦争の実態や残虐行為を知ってしまう。正義感に突き動かされたヘルムスは親友2人を仲間に加え、国家の嘘を暴くビラを町中に配布し、人々に真実を伝えていく。しかしその行為は、死刑に値する反逆罪だった。秘密国家警察の捜査が迫るなか、彼らの勇気ある行動は逃れられない運命へと突き進んでいく。 2002年にヘルムス・ヒューブナーの実像に迫ったドキュメンタリー作品を手がけたマット・ウィテカーが監督・脚本・製作を手がけ、同作の取材成果をもとに物語を再構築し劇映画として完成させた。

年齢を考慮せずともほんとうに強い！それは確信・信念なのか、信仰なのか、思い込みなのか、とにかく強い。友だちを見ると裏切れない人柄である。 そういうふうに生きてみたいし、その強さの秘密を知りたい。あるいはフランスの高校生が政府と対峙して時には暴力も否定せず行動することに通底しているのだろうか？ ただ、複雑な物事を理解するために、わかりやすく単純化してしまうことで生じる強さでなかったことを祈るばかりである。母は息子に生きてほしかっただろうと思う。 ヒットラーが主題というより、独裁や政治システムが生む戦争否定であり、国民を家畜のように扱う問題と自己家畜化する国民がテーマだったのかもしれない。

圧倒的な武力と監視体制を敷くナチスに対し、 言葉という武器だけで挑んだ彼らの姿は、 人間の尊厳とは何かを強く訴えかけてきます。 結末を知っていてもなお、 彼らの無事を祈らずにはいられないほど ストーリーに引き込まれました。 過去の歴史の悲劇として片付けるのではなく、 情報に溢れる現代社会において 真実を見極める目を持つことの大切さを突きつけられる、強いメッセージ性を持った素晴らしい作品。 劇中で描かれる彼らの葛藤や、 迫り来る危険への恐怖の描写が 非常にリアルで観ているこちらも 息が詰まるような緊張感がありました。 正しいことを正しいと言えなくなる 社会の恐ろしさを知ると同時に、 一歩を踏み出す勇気の重さを教えてくれる 現代にも深く通じる名作だと感じます。

"荣获杰出艺术家奖的汉森发表了该活动中最具情感的演讲之一，她反思了自己在业内度过的二十多年时光，以及她希望利用自己的平台为他人服务的愿望。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "在 Deadline 上观看", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我祈求上帝使用我，在无声震耳欲聋的地方，让我成为那些看不见的人的发言人，”她说。“如果我必须穿上铠甲，求求上帝，让它去保护别人的尊严，而不仅仅是我自己的。”汉森反思了她作为有色人种演员的不懈工作，并指出她用来为其他受虐待的有色人种发声的铠甲既能保护社区，也能“将其隔离开来”。汉森继续说道：“通过艺术、倡导、慈善和创业，我选择用我的铠甲来捍卫尊严、创造可能性，并提醒人们治愈和快乐是我们的天生权利。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她以向在充满问题和歧视的行业中工作的艺术家传达的信息结束了演讲：“最坚强的人不是我们这些筑墙的人，最坚强的人是那些有勇气打破高墙的人。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "荣获选角远见奖的芬恩对创作过程提出了不同的看法，她回顾了近三十年来寻找合适的演员来融入电影制片人想象的世界的经历。“我感到非常幸运，能拥有这样一份职业：每天的主题都是寻找潜力和展望一个尚未存在的未来，”她说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她接着解释说，选角导演的任务是在演员和角色之间找到完美的契合，包括在艺术家们一块块构建群戏时他们之间潜在的化学反应。“我们坐在前排，帮助演员成长，协助他们创作，支持他们大放异彩，从而让他们成为明星，”芬恩说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她也迅速承认，这项工作从来不是孤军奋战，她将自己职业生涯背后的努力归功于她的同事和助理，并代表更广泛的选角群体接受了这一荣誉。“选角导演是梦想家。我们是行动派。我们是寻宝者。在摄像机开拍之前，我们就已经开始构想各种可能性。我们都是有远见的人，我非常荣幸能代表我勇敢而杰出的选角群体接受这个奖项，”她说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "上午与《Variety》杂志的10位备受瞩目的演员的对话也让人得以一窥表演者对待其手艺的不同方式，几位演员在应对描绘难以简单归类的复杂人物这一挑战时找到了共鸣。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因饰演《Misty Green》而获得认可的罗莎琳德·伊莱扎尔表示，她被那些“有点难以去爱、难以去支持”的角色所吸引。这位演员称赞克里斯·洛克的剧本无所畏惧，并将她的角色描述为充满矛盾、自我毁灭且容易做出糟糕决定的人。", "links": [{"text": "Rosalind Eleazar", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/rosalind-eleazar/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对伊莱扎尔而言，挑战在于理解是什么驱使一个人会有这种行为。“我很感兴趣，为什么会有人以她那种充满挑衅的方式闯入世界？”她说。“很显然，通常这源于痛苦和苦难。所以实际上，能饰演这样一个角色真是一份厚礼。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在《成为休曼》中主演的露丝·马德利在塑造残疾人权利活动家朱迪·休曼时，发现了另一种复杂性。马德利表示，这段经历让她在了解休曼作为运动中强大人物的地位之外，还能更多地了解她的人性，包括她的快乐与不确定性。她还指出残疾人在电影和电视中担当主角的重要意义。“[这部电影证明了]残疾人可以在行业顶端引领故事，”马德利说。", "links": [{"text": "Ruth Madeley", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/ruth-madeley/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《痴迷》主演因德·纳瓦雷特呼应了伊莱扎尔对多维度角色的兴趣，她描述了尽管剧本中台词有限，但要让尼基显得血肉丰满所面临的挑战。这位演员表示，她惊奇地发现，那些在看到该角色后找到她的女性在尼基身上看到了自己的影子。纳瓦雷特说：“我发现不仅女性身上存在复杂性，我们作为人本身也存在复杂性，即我们具有多面性，这很美妙，我非常荣幸能饰演她。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "与此同时，电影节的国际才俊们也分享了他们对电影制作学习曲线的看法。玛丽安娜·迪·吉罗拉莫和吉塔里卡德拉富恩特都是首次出演电影的西班牙语表演者，他们讨论了与各自角色的共情以及与大牌明星合作的感受。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "出演马丁·麦克唐纳（Martin McDonagh）《Wild Horse Nine》的迪·吉罗拉莫（Di Girolamo）坦言，首次用英语表演是一大挑战，尤其是考虑到这位电影人独特的编剧风格。她解释说，麦克唐纳标志性的黑色幽默和才华——即“他的语言”——让她能够处理一些对自己而言极为贴近现实的题材，也就是该片取材于1973年智利推翻社会主义总统萨尔瓦多·阿连德（Salvador Allende）政变的情节。她感谢了方言教练佩妮（Penny）、麦克唐纳以及联合主演约翰·马尔科维奇（John Malkovich）和山姆·洛克威尔（Sam Rockwell）对她整个过程的帮助。她补充说，在复活节岛（Rapa Nui）上的拍摄经历让这段经历更加令人难忘。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Guitarricadelafuente表示，他最初对参演《La Bola Negra》的前景感到恐惧。他解释说，作为一名音乐人，在舞台上表演能让他采用不同的化身，展现自己向往的一面。然而，饰演塞巴斯蒂安（Sebastian）则需要一种不同层面的内省。“这不仅来自导演们盲目的信任以及他们显而易见的才华，而且突然之间，你不再需要去刻画一个化身，而是必须通过这个角色去直面你自己以及你内心深处的东西，”他说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部电影以西班牙内战及诗人费德里科·加西亚·洛尔卡（Federico García Lorca）的遗产为背景，交织了3个酷儿故事，让他在第一部表演作品中得以探索艰难的题材。他还对能与佩内洛普·克鲁兹（Penélope Cruz）合作表示感激，称这段经历“简直不可思议”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "今年电影节荣誉奖的其他得主包括：获得杰出表演成就奖（Outstanding Achievement in Acting Award）的杰克·奥康奈尔（Jack O’Connell）；获得聚光灯奖（Spotlight Award）的麦肯娜·格瑞丝（Mckenna Grace）；以及凭家庭电影获得突破奖（Breakout Award for Family Movie）的索西·贝肯（Sosie Bacon）。《综艺》杂志“10大瞩目演员”的其他成员还包括埃斯梅·克里德-迈尔斯（Esmé Creed-Miles，《理智与情感》）、萨默·H·豪厄尔（Summer H. Howell，《魔女嘉莉》）、贾法尔·杰克逊（Jaafar Jackson，《迈克尔》）、雷·尼科尔森（Ray Nicholson，《The Mosquito Bowl》）和约瑟夫·扎达（Joseph Zada，《伊甸园之东》）。", "links": [{"text": "Sosie Bacon", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/sosie-bacon/"}, {"text": "Jaafar Jackson", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/jaafar-jackson/"}, {"text": "East of Eden", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/east-of-eden/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "第27届纽波特海滩电影节于10月15日至22日在南加州举行。", "translated": true}]

"text": "“I asked God to use me and to use me as a voice for the unseen where silence was deafening,” she said. “If I had to wear armor, please God, let it protect somebody else’s humanity, not just mine.” Reflecting on her tireless work as an actor of color, Henson noted that the armor she uses to speak up for other mistreated people of color can both protect and “separate” communities. article_text:
Taraji P. Henson reflected on the power of art to defend dignity and create possibility, while casting director Sarah Finn celebrated the collaborative work behind bringing stories to life at the Newport Beach Film Festival ’s 27th annual Festival Honors brunch.

Held Oct. 18 at Balboa Bay Resort, the event brought together Hollywood veterans and emerging talent for a celebration of the artists and craftspeople helping shape the coming awards season. The morning began with Variety’s 10 Actors to Watch, a group of performers discussing their experiences on films spanning independent features, international productions and major studio releases, before the festival turned to its honorees.

Related Stories

Chris Rock, Quinta Brunson, Jaafar Jackson, Chiwetel Ejiofor Among Honorees For 9th Critics Choice Celebration Of Black Cinema & TV

'Being Heumann' Trailer: First Extended Look At Siân Heder's 'CODA' Follow-Up

Henson, who received the Artist of Distinction Award, delivered one of the event’s most emotional speeches, reflecting on more than two decades in the industry and her desire to use her platform to serve others.

Watch on Deadline

“I asked God to use me and to use me as a voice for the unseen where silence was deafening,” she said. “If I had to wear armor, please God, let it protect somebody else’s humanity, not just mine.” Reflecting on her tireless work as an actor of color, Henson noted that the armor she uses to speak up for other mistreated people of color can both protect and “separate” communities. Henson continued: “Through art, advocacy, philanthropy, and entrepreneurship, I choose to use mine to defend dignity, create possibility, and remind people that healing and joy are our birthright.”

She closed with a message for artists working in an industry dotted with troubles and discrimination: “The strongest people aren’t those of us who build walls, but the strongest people are the ones who have the courage to knock them down.”

Finn, who received the Casting Visionary Award, offered a different perspective on the creative process, reflecting on nearly three decades spent finding the right actors to inhabit the worlds filmmakers imagine. “I feel very lucky to have a career where every day it’s all about looking for potential and envisioning a future that doesn’t exist yet.” she said.

Continuing, she explained that casting directors are tasked with finding the right match between an actor and a role, including potential chemistry between artists as they build an ensemble piece by piece. “We are in the front row, helping actors grow, helping them create, supporting them to shine so they can become stars,” Finn said.

She was also quick to acknowledge that the work is never done alone, crediting her associates and assistants for the effort behind her career and accepting the honor on behalf of the wider casting community. Casting directors are dreamers. We are doers. We are treasure hunters. We start imagining possibility before the camera rolls. We are all visionaries, and I’m so proud to accept this award on behalf of my bold and brilliant casting community,” she said.

The morning’s conversations with Variety’s 10 Actors to Watch also offered a glimpse at the different ways performers approach their craft, with several finding common ground in the challenge of portraying complicated people who resist easy categorization.

Rosalind Eleazar , recognized for Misty Green , said she is drawn to characters who are “somewhat difficult to love and difficult to back.” The actor praised Chris Rock’s writing as fearless, describing her character as contradictory, self-destructive and prone to terrible decisions.

For Eleazar, the challenge was understanding what might drive someone to behave that way. “I’m interested in why does someone come out into the world punching the way she does?” she said. “And obviously, usually that comes from a source of pain and suffering. So really, it was a gift of a character to play.”

Ruth Madeley , who stars in Being Heumann , found a different kind of complexity in portraying disability rights activist Judy Heumann. Madeley said the experience allowed her to learn more about Heumann’s humanity, including her joy and uncertainty, beyond her status as a formidable figure in the movement. She also pointed to the significance of disabled people taking leading roles in film and television. “[This film proves] that disabled people can lead stories at the top of the industry,” Madeley said.

Obsession star Inde Navarrette echoed Eleazar’s interest in multidimensional characters, describing the challenge of making Nikki feel fully formed despite having limited words on the page. The actor said she was struck by how women who approached her after seeing the character recognized themselves in Nikki. I find that there’s a complexity, not just in women, but in us as people where we are multiple people and that’s beautiful and I was very honored to portray her,” Navarrette said.

Meanwhile, the festival’s international talent offered their perspective on the learning curve of filmmaking. Mariana Di Girolamo and Guitarricadelafuente, both Spanish-speaking performers debuting in their first films, discussed relating to their characters and working alongside big names.

Di Girolamo, who appears in Martin McDonagh’s Wild Horse Nine , described performing in English for the first time as a challenge, particularly given the filmmaker’s distinctive writing style. She explained that McDonagh’s notably dark humor and wit, “his language,” allowed him to address subjects close to home for her, namely the film’s plot, which is based on Chile’s 1973 coup to overthrow socialist president Salvador Allende. She credited her dialect coach, Penny, along with McDonagh and co-stars John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell, with helping her through the process. Filming on Rapa Nui, she added, made the experience all the more memorable.

Guitarricadelafuente said he was initially frightened by the prospect of acting in La Bola Negra . He explained that as a musician, performing onstage allows him to adopt alter egos and inhabit aspirational versions of himself. Playing Sebastian, however, required a different kind of introspection. “It was not just the blind faith from the directors and obviously the talent, their talent in them, but suddenly there was this thing of not having to portray an alter ego, but having to confront yourself and your inner things with this character,” he said.

The film, which intertwines three queer stories against the backdrop of the Spanish Civil War and the legacy of poet Federico García Lorca, allowed him to explore difficult subjects in his first acting role. He also expressed gratitude for the chance to work alongside Penélope Cruz, calling the experience “just out of this world.”

Other recipients of this year’s Festival Honors included Jack O’Connell, who received the Outstanding Achievement in Acting Award; Mckenna Grace, recipient of the Spotlight Award; and Sosie Bacon , who received the Breakout Award for Family Movie . The remaining members of Variety’s 10 Actors to Watch were Esmé Creed-Miles ( Sense and Sensibility ), Summer H. Howell ( Carrie ), Jaafar Jackson ( Michael ), Ray Nicholson ( The Mosquito Bowl ) and Joseph Zada ( East of Eden ).

The 27th annual Newport Beach Film Festival runs Oct. 15–22 in Southern California.

article_text:
Die Kunst der Woche in Basel, Berlin, Dresden, Esch-sur-Alzette, Frankfurt am Main, Leipzig und Wiesbaden

Ruth Asawa in Basel

Sie sehen aus wie Kokons, Blüten oder seltsame Meeresbewohner und scheinen beinahe schwerelos im Raum zu schweben. Dabei bestehen Ruth Asawas Skulpturen aus ganz gewöhnlichem Draht. Die Technik, mit der die US-amerikanische Künstlerin ihre filigranen Gebilde formte, lernte sie 1947 auf einer Reise nach Mexiko kennen. Dort ließ sie sich von traditionellen Drahtkörben inspirieren, später entwickelte sie daraus immer komplexere Formen.

Asawa, die während des Zweiten Weltkriegs als Jugendliche mit ihrer japanischstämmigen Familie in einem US-Internierungslager festgehalten wurde, studierte anschließend am legendären Black Mountain College bei Josef Albers. Zu ihrem 100. Geburtstag widmet die Fondation Beyeler der 2013 verstorbenen Künstlerin ihre erste europäische Retrospektive. Über 200 Werke, darunter Skulpturen, Zeichnungen und Papierarbeiten, zeigen, wie sie sich über sechs Jahrzehnte mit einfachen Materialien und den Formen der Natur beschäftigte.

"Ruth Asawa" , Fondation Beyeler, Riehen/Basel, bis 10. Januar 2027

Peter Wächtler in Berlin

Der 1979 in Hannover geborene Peter Wächtler schreibt, filmt, zeichnet, malt, baut Skulpturen und Filmsets, um vertraute Genres und Erzählweisen in eine Balance von Nostalgie, Tragik und absurdem Humor zu überführen. In zwei Jahrzehnten hat Wächtler eine eigene Formensprache entwickelt, die mit der Geschichte spielt, um gegenwärtige Widersprüche zwischen Selbstbestimmung und Selbstaufgabe miteinander zu verschränken. Nun präsentiert das Haus am Waldsee Wächtlers erste umfassende institutionelle Soloschau in Berlin. Neben einer neuen Filmproduktion sind ortsspezifische Arbeiten entstanden, die in einen Dialog mit der Architektur des Hauses treten.

Peter Wächtler "Ständig" , Haus am Waldsee, Berlin, bis 17. Januar 2027

Beuys in Dresden

Als passionierter Zeichner verstand sich Joseph Beuys (1921-1986) wirklich als "Sender". Denn insbesondere das Medium der Zeichnung vermag Gedanken und Energien zu vermitteln. Für Beuys waren Zeichnungen zwar auch Darstellungsformen, vor allem aber "Denkformen", die komplexe Verbindungen zwischen Natur, Materie und Gesellschaft zugänglich machen. Die Ausstellung im Dresdner Kupferstich-Kabinett präsentiert über 100 zwischen 1945 und 1985 entstandene Zeichnungen aus der Sammlung Aeneas Bastian.

"Ich bin ein Sender … Die Zeichnungen von Joseph Beuys" , Kupferstich-Kabinett im Residenzschloss, Dresden, bis 17. Januar 2027

Ruinen in Esch-sur-Alzette

Statt als nostalgisches Überbleibsel lässt sich die Ruine auch als Raum kritischer Auseinandersetzung betrachten. Die Ausstellung "Ruin Echoes" in der Kunsthalle im luxemburgischen Esch-sur-Alzette betrachtet die Ruine als Ort der Spannung – materiell, symbolisch und politisch – und setzt sich mit der Entropie auseinander, jenem unvermeidlichen Prozess des Zerfalls, der Strukturen, Regime und Erinnerungen ergreift. In ihren Filmen, Skulpturen, Installationen und Fotoarbeiten betrachten die beteiligten Kunstschaffenden Ruinen nicht als Endpunkte, sondern als mögliche Anfänge. Dabei sind unter anderen Laurenz Berges, David Claerbout, Asta Gröting, Gregor Hildebrandt, Hiwa K, Maya Schweizer und Clemens von Wedemeyer.

"Ruin Echoes" , Konschthal Esch, 24. Oktober bis 14. Februar 2027

Leonor Fini in Frankfurt am Main

In den Gemälden von Leonor Fini haben meistens die Frauen das Sagen. Die 1907 in Buenos Aires geborene Künstlerin bewegte sich im Umfeld der Surrealisten, wollte sich der Bewegung aber nie offiziell anschließen. Lieber erfand sie ihre eigene Welt aus Mythen, Erotik und eigenwilligen Geschlechterrollen. Frauen treten darin als mächtige Priesterinnen oder rätselhafte Mischwesen auf, während Männer auch mal nackt und wehrlos zu ihren Füßen liegen.

Fini liebte außerdem die große Inszenierung: Sie entwarf Kostüme für Oper und Theater und verwandelte sich selbst mit Masken, Federn und Hörnern in Figuren, die ebenso gut aus ihren Bildern stammen könnten. Die Schirn Kunsthalle Frankfurt widmet der 1996 verstorbenen Künstlerin nun ihre erste Retrospektive in Deutschland. Zu sehen sind rund 100 Werke, darunter Gemälde, Zeichnungen, Fotografien und Kostüme.

Leonor Fini "Magisch surreal" , Schirn Kunsthalle, Frankfurt am Main, bis 21. Februar 2027

Grassimesse in Leipzig

Schmuck, Keramik, Glas und Textil: Rund 140 Künstler, Designer und Kunsthandwerker von mehreren Kontinenten verkaufen am Wochenende im Leipziger Grassi Museum ihre Arbeiten. Auf der Grassimesse stehen renommierte Gestalter neben jungen Kunsthandwerkern und Hochschulabsolventen, wie das Museum mitteilte. Die Aussteller kommen aus Europa, Südamerika und Ostasien.

Die Messe lädt zum Schauen, Informieren und Kaufen ein. Neue Gestaltungstrends stehen im Mittelpunkt: So präsentieren etwa junge Produktdesigner neue Materialkombinationen und Schuhdesigner stellen ihre neuesten Kollektionen vor. Es gibt Arbeiten aus verschiedensten Bereichen des Kunsthandwerks und des Designs. Auch hochwertige Unikate und Kleinserien stehen zum Verkauf.

Zudem wurden acht Grassipreise vergeben. Die am höchsten dotierten Auszeichnungen gingen an zwei deutsche Künstlerinnen: Für ihre präzise gearbeitete Gebrauchskunst bekam die Silberschmiedin Beata Leonards den Grassipreis des Carl und Anneliese Goerdeler Stiftungsfonds – er ist mit 3000 Euro dotiert. Den mit einem Sachpreis im Wert von 4000 Euro verbundenen Gemma Grassipreis erhielt die Schmuckgestalterin Margit Jäschke. Eine Fachjury wählte die Gewinner aus den 140 teilnehmenden Künstlern aus. (dpa/Monopol)

Grassimesse , Grassi Museum, Leipzig, bis 25. Oktober

Blaue Reiterinnen in Wiesbaden

Die Künstlerinnen und Künstler des "Blauen Reiter" waren wichtige Protagonisten der Avantgardebewegungen vor dem Ersten Weltkrieg. Im Fokus waren bislang vor allem ihre männlichen Mitglieder der Gruppe wie Wassily Kandinsky und Franz Marc, Paul Klee und August Macke. Das internationale Ausstellungsprojekt "Die Blauen Reiterinnen" richtet den Blick nun auf die Frauen aus der Künstlergruppe, darunter Gabriele Münter und Marianne von Werefkin.

Die Premiere ist im Landesmuseum Wiesbaden, wo über 140 Werke von zwölf Pionierinnen der Moderne gezeigt werden. Die Ausstellung erzähle die Geschichte der Gruppe konsequent aus der Perspektive der Künstlerinnen, so das Museum. Damit werde Sichtbarkeit für diejenigen geschaffen, die nach dem Zweiten Weltkrieg im Kontext der Gruppe weitestgehend unbeachtet blieben. Bis heute sei nahezu unerforscht, welch großen Anteil die Frauen an der Entwicklung der Moderne hatten oder welche Strategien und Netzwerke sie nutzten. (dpa/Monopol)

"Die Blauen Reiterinnen" , Museum Wiesbaden, bis 21. Februar 2027
